title: Ship a side project in one weekend

slides.heading: Ship a side project this weekend
slides.body: Most side projects die in week three. Here is the scope that survives to Sunday night.

slides.heading: Pick something you can describe in one line
slides.body: If the pitch needs a paragraph, the build needs a month. Cut until one sentence covers it.

slides.heading: Write the ending first
slides.body: Decide exactly what "done" looks like on Sunday at 6pm. Everything outside that is version two.

slides.heading: Use the boring stack you know
slides.body: A weekend is not the time to learn a framework. Reach for the tools your hands already know.

slides.heading: Deploy before you build
slides.subtitle: Hello world, in production
slides.body: Get an empty page live in the first hour. Deployment surprises are cheap on Friday, fatal on Sunday.

slides.heading: Fake the hard part
slides.body: Hardcode it. Stub it. Fill it by hand. Prove people want the thing before you automate the thing.
bullets: Static JSON instead of a database
A form that emails you instead of a dashboard
You, manually, instead of a cron job

slides.heading: No accounts until someone asks
slides.body: Auth is a weekend on its own. Ship without login and watch whether anyone misses it.

slides.heading: Timebox the design to one hour
slides.body: Pick two fonts and three colours, then stop. Consistency reads as design. Fiddling reads as delay.

slides.heading: Post it before it is ready
slides.body: Sunday night, unfinished, with a caveat. Feedback on a live thing beats a polished thing nobody saw.

slides.heading: What are you shipping this weekend?
slides.body: Reply with the one-line pitch. I will tell you what to cut.
